text: 🇲🇽🌎 "There will be a bilateral meeting with the government of China, with the President of China." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Sheinbaum confirmed her trip to the APEC summit in China. She leaves early Sunday, Nov 15, and is back by Nov 20; the Interior Secretary will host the mañaneras that week. Several bilateral meetings are being arranged, including one with President Xi Jinping and Chinese ministers. It is not yet confirmed that Trump will attend: "If he goes, of course, we're interested in meeting with him." A day earlier, she said Mexico has a very good relationship with both China and the United States.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "A good part of the Hernández Casillas companies are coyotes. They don't even produce. They are intermediary companies." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Sheinbaum announced a decree next week to strengthen Talleres Gráficos de México, the state printer that makes the federal ballots, "so that most electoral materials are made in the Mexican state's company." Its board, now just the Interior, Anti-Corruption and Finance ministries, will add more ministries, the Superior Audit Office as an observer, and academics from UNAM, IPN or Tec de Monterrey. For ballot boxes and voting screens, she called for open bidding with clear guidelines and unit prices, so that one state doesn't pay ten times what another pays for the same thing. The Superior Audit Office will audit every state electoral body.

🇲🇽📉 <u>Banxico Surprises: Rate Cut to 6.25%</u>

Banco de México cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6.25% on Thursday, by majority vote, after holding at 6.50% since May. The market expected no change. El Financiero notes that Banxico had already said it would not "copy" the Fed. The rate gap with the US was at a record low of 250 basis points.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum Moves Ballot Printing Back to the State</u>

After exposing a network of family firms that held INE and state electoral contracts for 27 years, worth more than 2.6 billion pesos, Sheinbaum announced a decree requiring Talleres Gráficos de México, the state printer, to produce most official election materials. The ASF will act as an observer, with academics taking part. Ballot boxes and voting booths will go to Mexican firms through bids with clear prices and a chain of custody. "This didn't start with Taddei," she said.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum Confirms China Trip: APEC and a Meeting with Xi</u>

Sheinbaum confirmed she will travel to China from November 15 to 20 for the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen, her first trip there since taking office. A bilateral meeting with Xi Jinping is set, with both cabinets taking part. If Trump shows up, she said she is open to seeing him too. A day earlier she said the trade relationship with the US does not stop Mexico from dealing with China.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexico Rejects US Blockade of Cuba at Ibero-American Summit</u>

At the XXX Ibero-American Summit in Madrid, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco used the plenary to restate Mexico's "historical position of rejection of the embargo and other coercive economic measures against Cuba." He framed Mexico's security cooperation with any nation around four principles, ending with "cooperation without subordination."

🇲🇽✈️ <u>AICM pays off $566M of Texcoco airport debt</u>

On November 2, Mexico City's airport paid $565.9 million to fully retire the 2026 notes issued for the cancelled Texcoco airport, El Financiero reports. The remaining $3.152 billion will be covered from AICM's own operating revenue. The payoff came from recovered passenger traffic, a stronger peso and more operations per hour.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>Harfuch: two years in, "a very different situation"</u>

At a ceremony honoring security personnel on the government's second anniversary, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch gave the credit to Sheinbaum, who personally runs the security strategy and reviews crime data every day at 6 a.m. In three operations since 2025, Mexico has transferred 92 cartel figures to the US. Some of them had avoided extradition for up to 40 years, through three or four previous administrations. "Today, thanks to the President's leadership, the country's security is changing."

🇲🇽📚 <u>Phones off, books open: SEP's plan for the school phone ban</u>

With the cellphone restriction now in force in primary and secondary schools, the SEP launched two campaigns, "Turn off your phone, turn on your imagination" and "Read", to explain the ban to students and expand school libraries. Sheinbaum on scrolling: "It's like a drug, because they put the phone down and crave picking it back up, and they feel empty." Education Secretary Mario Delgado: "If they're going to get hooked, let it be on books, not the screen."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Samuel García reported to the FGR for organized crime</u>

Morena's Nuevo León coordinator Clara Luz Flores, joined by Senator Alejandro Murat and Deputy Alfonso Ramírez Cuéllar, filed a criminal complaint with the FGR against Governor Samuel García, his wife Mariana Rodríguez and his father for organized crime, embezzlement, illicit enrichment and money laundering. The core accusation is that more than 7 billion pesos in public money went through a network of companies tied to a law firm in the governor's family circle. Monterrey's PRI mayor Adrián de la Garza is also named. Across both administrations, more than 14 billion pesos in public funds are at stake.
